narrative.title: Slotting Adjoaining Workstations for Assembly Cells
narrative.scenario: A factory installs stations along one row, each coming online on a known day. An assembly cell needs k neighbouring stations active, and production requires m such cells. Find the first day on which the floor can field m cells, or admit that the row is too short to ever do it.
narrative.inputFormat: An array bloomDay of n integers (the day each station comes online), an integer m (cells required) and an integer k (adjacent stations per cell).
narrative.outputFormat: The minimum day on which m bouquets of k adjacent bloomed stations can be formed, or -1 when fewer than m * k stations exist.

complexity.optimalTime: O(n log D), where D is the latest bloom day

testCases.explanation: By day 3 the stations at positions 1, 3 and 5 have come online, giving three single-station cells.
Day 7 offers only one run of four adjacent stations; waiting for day 12 lights the whole row, enough for two cells.

hintLevels: Level 1: Feasibility is monotonic in the day - once m cells can be fielded, waiting longer never loses them.
Level 2: For a candidate day, sweep the row tallying runs of consecutive available stations and count how many full k-runs they contain.

Level 3: The run counter must reset whenever a station is still offline, the feasibility scan needs a wide type when multiplying m by k, and a row shorter than m * k stations fails before any search starts.
